acceptance_criteria.criterion: The record states the argument the events lane actually made, rather than a paraphrase: both pre-existing checks at the same boundary already fail open, so failing only the new check closed would reject requests the other two would have allowed. The decision either accepts that reasoning or answers it.
evidence: VENUE-D07 Evidence 1 states the argument in the events lane's own mechanical form and concedes its factual core: 'All three checks in validateVenueAvailability fail open on a read error' — block check route.ts:99-118; capacity read :120-126 destructures only { data: venue } so a failed read yields venue === null, capacity computes to 0, and capacity > 0 (:127) is false; approved-booking read :142-150 destructures only { count } so a failed read yields count === null and count || 0 is 0. 'The lane is right that flipping only the new check closed would reject requests the other two would have allowed.'

Every one of those claims was verified against the current bytes rather than taken from the events lane's record; the capacity and count destructuring are quoted from the file as read, not from EVENTS-002.json.

The reasoning is then ANSWERED, not adopted, in Evidence 3: two accidental violations are not a rule, and the neighbours are not equivalent — the approved-booking count is more dangerous to fail open than the block check because it misses a conflict with an already-promised booking. 'The inconsistency is the defect to fix; the fix is to classify the checks, not to freeze the worst behaviour in place.'

The answer is strengthened with a FOURTH read the events lane did not name (Evidence 2): the venue policy read at :327-332 also discards `error`, and readVenueBookingPolicies computes allowBookings: s.allow_bookings !== false at :78, so a transient read error sets allowBookings to TRUE and inverts the venue's explicit 'not accepting booking requests' switch (:334-339). A permission gate failing open toward permissive is worse than either read the events lane named.

The severity leg of the events lane's argument is answered specifically, not waved at (Evidence 4): 'the venue manager still reviews and approves it' is FALSE for booking_policies.auto_approve = 'all', because route.ts:365 sets initialStatus = 'approved' at request time with no human in the loop; and the reservation conflict engine does not guard this path because it constrains venue_reservations (20260823140000_reservation_conflict_engine.sql:92-99), a different table, is recorded as staged/not applied, and is gated behind isVenueBookingLifecycleEnabled() with a 503 at app/api/venue/booking-requests/route.ts:118-128.

The ruling that carries the decision is that the fail-closed PRINCIPLE is granted and its application refused, for one stated reason (Evidence 6): 'this boundary is where the request is formed, not where the promise is kept'. Evidence 5 measures that there is no second machine check — app/api/venue/booking-requests/route.ts:106-203 reads only venue_booking_requests and calls transition_venue_booking_lifecycle, never consulting venue_availability.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The decision states the blast radius of failing closed: a transient availability read error would deny booking requests to paying artists on sellable dates, which is a revenue-visible failure mode and not a neutral one. The cost of each posture is named in the record.
evidence: VENUE-D07 has a dedicated 'Blast radius — the cost of each posture, named' section, and both postures get a full paragraph rather than a one-line summary.

FAIL-CLOSED cost, stated: one transient read error denies 100% of venue-targeted booking requests for the duration — every venue, every date, no discrimination — because this is the highest-fan-out read in the function and it runs first. Revenue-visible and misattributed: 'the artist is told a specific date is unavailable at a named venue, which is false and suppresses the venue's own book; artists re-date or abandon and the venue never learns a sale was lost to an infrastructure error.' Also: invisible in the response (a 409 is indistinguishable from a genuine conflict, so no client can detect it, no retry affordance exists, nothing alerts on the 409 path); not self-healing for the artist (a retry on the same date returns a different answer, so the same input yields contradictory facts); not scopeable down by venue; and the guarantee is held 'by an outage' and released by recovery, 'which is backwards'.

FAIL-OPEN cost, stated with equal specificity: a manager's block can be ignored for the duration of the read failure and the request carries no signal that the date was blocked — 'the request's own record asserts the date is open'; the harm is concentrated in the auto_approve = 'all' case where fail-open is 'not a request the venue can decline but a block silently overridden'; it is recoverable and attributable (logged at :116, lands in a human queue); and it is not security-relevant, because the check is service-role scoped to input.venueId and is not an authorization gate, contrasted with VENUE-D01 where fail-closed was required precisely because that surface IS the authorization gate.

Neither cost is rounded to zero: the record states explicitly 'Neither cost is neutral', and it records the deciding asymmetry — the fail-closed failure mode is invisible to BOTH parties and attributes an infrastructure fault to a business fact, while the fail-open failure mode is visible to the operator, logged, and correctable by the human already in the loop.

The mechanism that makes the fail-closed cost concrete is pinned (Evidence 7): the block check runs first at :99, ahead of the capacity read, so the artist receives 409 'The venue is not available on 2026-10-15' for a date the venue never blocked, and 'the 409 vocabulary is a business-fact vocabulary and has no way to say we could not confirm'.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The conditions under which fail-closed becomes correct are stated, so the posture is a decision with a re-evaluation trigger rather than a permanent preference. At minimum: what has to be true about read reliability for the safer posture to become the right one.
evidence: VENUE-D07 has a dedicated 'Re-evaluation triggers' section with five falsifiable triggers (R1-R5), framed as 'fail-closed becomes correct, and this decision must be re-opened, if ANY of these becomes true' — an explicit re-evaluation trigger, not a permanent preference.

R2 is the required read-reliability condition and is stated quantitatively: the specific query (venue_availability .eq(venue_id).eq(date).eq(is_available,false).maybeSingle(), lib/venue/availability.ts:129-135) must have a MEASURED error rate on a hosted environment, and the expected number of falsely-denied artist requests per unit time must be lower than the expected number of block overrides per unit time. The record states plainly that no such measurement exists in this repository and no hosted evidence is claimed, so the trigger cannot be evaluated today — it is a real condition, not a rhetorical hedge.

R1 (a block check at the promise point: the venue-side approval path or the applied reservation engine) is named as the near-term trigger AND as the debt this decision creates — 'it should be opened regardless of which posture holds' — so the ratification is not read as excusing the gap.

R3 states the condition under which the safer posture stops being a lie: a flipped posture must return a retryable infrastructure error (e.g. 503 with a RETRY code) and must NOT reuse the 409 'venue is not available on <date>' vocabulary. 'If that 409 vocabulary is the only one available, fail-closed is not a posture, it is a lie with a status code.'

R4 voids the human-review mitigation for auto_approve = 'all' (:365) and requires re-evaluation if auto-approve is reachable in production or any other path can reach 'approved' without a human. R5 makes the permissive permission-gate reads a precondition, since 'a strict advisory check sitting behind an open permission gate is the worst of both worlds'.

checkpoints.summary: VENUE-007 complete, all five ACs met. Decided fail-open-and-log for a block read error at the booking boundary; recorded as VENUE-D07 in the venue lane's own log, dated and attributed to venue as contract owner. The events lane did the right thing by flagging rather than smoothing, and the ratification confirms its implementation rather than re-doing it: app/api/booking-requests/route.ts was not touched. What I did not do is accept its reasoning by default. Its decisive factual claim verified CORRECT against current bytes — all three checks fail open — and I said so plainly in the decision rather than looking for a way to disagree. But I answered the argument: two accidental violations are not a rule, the approved-booking count is MORE dangerous to fail open than the check I would have flipped, and a fourth read neither lane had named (the allow_bookings policy read) fails open in the permissive direction, inverting an operator's explicit 'not accepting bookings' switch. That produced the decision's reusable rule — decide by whether a check narrows or gates, not by what the neighbours do — and it also produced a new fail-closed task, which is the opposite of what my own handoff originally asked for. Recorded the blast radius of both postures without rounding either down, including the specific reason fail-closed is bad HERE: the block check runs first, so its failure mode is a confident 409 telling a paying artist a named venue is unavailable on a date it never blocked, and the 409 vocabulary has no way to say 'we could not confirm'. That is why R3 exists. Five falsification-grade triggers keep this from being a permanent preference, with R2 stating exactly what must be true about read reliability — a MEASURED error rate for this query — and stating plainly that no such measurement exists and none is claimed. Recorded honestly that the fail-open posture is only defensible because the request is not the promise, and that app/api/venue/booking-requests/route.ts:106-203 never consults venue_availability, so today there is no second machine check; that gap is the decision's named debt and is routed as R1. FIND-1 routed to the orchestrator as a candidate, not fixed and not renumbered, and not turned into a task record because that is outside the grant and would collide on the venue verification WIP slot. Annotated the handoff inside its existing schema fields (additionalProperties is false) and corrected its stale line references, which still claimed the function did not consult venue_availability — leaving those would have misled the next lane. Both gates green: 15 files / 131 tests, and 0 warnings / 0 errors strict. Append-only respected: 182 insertions, 0 deletions, D01-D06 untouched; an earlier mid-document insertion of my own was reverted with git checkout after confirming the file was clean at HEAD, so only my own edit was discarded. Nothing committed, nothing staged, no migration authored or applied.
